title: Existence of natural Roos comparison maps
statement: Let A be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with countable products, and I,J integer cochain complexes of towers [def-weil-inverse-system]. For a chain map u:I\to J choose termwise-product presentations P,PJ, kernel presentations L,LJ for the transition endomorphisms [def-weil-tower-transition-endomorphism], signed cones C,CJ with differential (y,x)\mapsto(-dy-sx,dx), and comparisons eta,etaJ with components (0,iota),(0,iJ). Put U_p=eP_p.hom \circ Pi.map(u_p) \circ ePJ_p.inv (composition read in traversal order). There exist chain maps lU:L\to LJ and cU:C\to CJ with lU etaJ=eta cU, lU_p iJ_p=iota_p U_p, and cU_{p+1} eCJ_p.hom=eC_p.hom diag(U_p,U_{p+1}). No reverse map or homotopy is assumed.

source.place: Existing docstring: agent-written naturality/homotopy extension of lem-weil-derived-limit-roos-complex; background Stacks Project Tag 070M.

proof.text: Define U_p by the product map of u conjugated through the given product isomorphisms. Product projections give its chain-map equation. Naturality with the tower transitions and towerTransitionEndomorphism_natural_backward give s U = U sJ.

Factor iota_p U_p through the limiting kernel fork hLJ_p. Monicity of iJ_q gives the chain-map equation for the resulting lU. Define cU in degree p+1 by the diagonal biproduct of U_p and U_(p+1). Check the signed differential after its two projections using the two commutation equations. Other differentials vanish by complex shape.
After eCJ_p.hom both sides of the comparison square have first component zero and second component iota_(p+1) U_(p+1). This proves the square as well as the specified kernel and cone components.

theorem roos_comparison_maps
    (A : Type u) [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A]
    [HasLimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ) A]
    (I J : CochainComplex (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A) ℤ)
    (u : I ⟶ J)
    (P L C : CochainComplex A ℤ)
    (eP : ∀ p : ℤ, P.X p ≅ ∏ᶜ (fun n : ℕ ↦ (I.X p).obj (Opposite.op n)))
    (hP : ∀ p q : ℤ, P.d p q ≫ (eP q).hom =
      (eP p).hom ≫ Limits.Pi.map (fun n ↦ (I.d p q).app (Opposite.op n)))
    (oneSubS : P ⟶ P)
    (hS : ∀ p : ℤ, oneSubS.f p = (eP p).hom ≫
      towerTransitionEndomorphism
        (fun n ↦ (I.X p).map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) ≫ (eP p).inv)
    (iota : L ⟶ P)
    (hKernel : ∀ p : ℤ, iota.f p ≫ oneSubS.f p = 0)
    (hL : ∀ p : ℤ, IsLimit (KernelFork.ofι (iota.f p) (hKernel p)))
    (eC : ∀ p : ℤ, C.X (p + 1) ≅ P.X p ⊞ P.X (p + 1))
    (hC : ∀ p : ℤ, C.d (p + 1) (p + 1 + 1) ≫ (eC (p + 1)).hom =
      (eC p).hom ≫ biprod.lift
        (-(biprod.fst ≫ P.d p (p + 1)) - biprod.snd ≫ oneSubS.f (p + 1))
        (biprod.snd ≫ P.d (p + 1) (p + 1 + 1)))
    (eta : L ⟶ C)
    (hEta : ∀ p : ℤ, eta.f (p + 1) ≫ (eC p).hom =
      biprod.lift 0 (iota.f (p + 1)))
    (PJ LJ CJ : CochainComplex A ℤ)
    (ePJ : ∀ p : ℤ, PJ.X p ≅ ∏ᶜ (fun n : ℕ ↦ (J.X p).obj (Opposite.op n)))
    (hPJ : ∀ p q : ℤ, PJ.d p q ≫ (ePJ q).hom =
      (ePJ p).hom ≫ Limits.Pi.map (fun n ↦ (J.d p q).app (Opposite.op n)))
    (sJ : PJ ⟶ PJ)
    (hSJ : ∀ p : ℤ, sJ.f p = (ePJ p).hom ≫
      towerTransitionEndomorphism
        (fun n ↦ (J.X p).map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) ≫ (ePJ p).inv)
    (iJ : LJ ⟶ PJ)
    (hKJ : ∀ p : ℤ, iJ.f p ≫ sJ.f p = 0)
    (hLJ : ∀ p : ℤ, IsLimit (KernelFork.ofι (iJ.f p) (hKJ p)))
    (eCJ : ∀ p : ℤ, CJ.X (p + 1) ≅ PJ.X p ⊞ PJ.X (p + 1))
    (hCJ : ∀ p : ℤ, CJ.d (p + 1) (p + 1 + 1) ≫ (eCJ (p + 1)).hom =
      (eCJ p).hom ≫ biprod.lift
        (-(biprod.fst ≫ PJ.d p (p + 1)) - biprod.snd ≫ sJ.f (p + 1))
        (biprod.snd ≫ PJ.d (p + 1) (p + 1 + 1)))
    (etaJ : LJ ⟶ CJ)
    (hEtaJ : ∀ p : ℤ, etaJ.f (p + 1) ≫ (eCJ p).hom =
      biprod.lift 0 (iJ.f (p + 1)))
    : ∃ (lU : L ⟶ LJ) (cU : C ⟶ CJ),
      lU ≫ etaJ = eta ≫ cU ∧
      (∀ p : ℤ, lU.f p ≫ iJ.f p = iota.f p ≫ (eP p).hom ≫
        Limits.Pi.map (fun n ↦ (u.f p).app (Opposite.op n)) ≫ (ePJ p).inv) ∧
      (∀ p : ℤ, cU.f (p + 1) ≫ (eCJ p).hom = (eC p).hom ≫ biprod.map
        ((eP p).hom ≫ Limits.Pi.map (fun n ↦ (u.f p).app (Opposite.op n)) ≫
          (ePJ p).inv)
        ((eP (p + 1)).hom ≫
          Limits.Pi.map (fun n ↦ (u.f (p + 1)).app (Opposite.op n)) ≫
          (ePJ (p + 1)).inv))
